title: Assigning Anchors by IoU
tagline: Detection is classification in disguise: every pre-placed anchor box asks 'is the object here?', and IoU thresholds supply the labels.
summary: An anchor-based detector tiles the image with a fixed grid of boxes at several scales and aspect ratios, then trains each one as a yes/no classifier. Drag a ground-truth box across the grid and watch every anchor light up positive, ignore, or negative by its IoU with the object. Move the two thresholds and the counts shift; the single best-matching anchor is always kept. This is how 'where is the object' becomes a per-anchor classification problem.
highlights: Drag a ground-truth box over a fixed field of anchors and see each one classified positive, ignore, or negative in real time.
Anchors come in several aspect ratios per location, so a wide object matches wide anchors and a tall one matches tall anchors.
Move the high and low IoU thresholds and watch the positive, ignore, and negative counts rebalance instantly.
The single highest-IoU anchor is always kept as positive, mirroring the RPN rule that guarantees every object has a match.
See why detection is really per-anchor classification plus box regression, not a mysterious 'where is it' oracle.
